purpose: Every fixture is synthetic. No real capture, identifier, title, participant, path, or destination appears in this corpus, and none ever may.

valid.note: An experimental kind. Namespaced so it can never collide with a future core kind, and not structurally routable.
Every required member and nothing else: occurred_at and metadata are both optional, and a meeting without them is still routable by kind.
A meeting carrying exactly the trusted metadata structural routing needs. Nothing here requires reading the transcript.
The same item re-emitted by a later run of a newer adapter. Provenance and payload.preserved_at differ; every item fact is identical, which is what makes this a replay rather than a second item.
A general capture. Its destination depends on what it means, so a consumer may read the payload once — the envelope itself does not carry it.
The same source item after an edit: identical intake_id, different content digest. A revision is legal and is distinguishable from a replay.
A second adapter, a different storage scheme, and an undeclared metadata name. A consumer ignores names it does not know, which is what makes adding one a non-breaking change.
Content identity under the second admitted digest algorithm. The intake identity algorithm is fixed regardless.

invalid.note: A truncated sha-256 digest. Length is checked against the named algorithm, not merely against the hex alphabet.
Every member individually legal, the whole past the envelope ceiling. The ceiling is what keeps an envelope cheap to log, queue and store however large the captured item is.
A fractional number. Excluded so canonical form is reproducible across languages without a float-formatting rule.
A well-formed identity that is not the one the source implies. An adapter that invents identities breaks deduplication silently.
A nested object in metadata. Structure there is how a payload gets smuggled in a piece at a time.
Metadata inflated past its ceiling by many small legal members — the realistic way content leaks into an envelope.
A camelCase, vendor-shaped metadata name. Vendor attributes belong in the preserved payload.
content and captured_at absent. Identity and revision both become unanswerable without them.
Three unrelated violations at once: validation reports all of them, not the first, so an adapter author fixes one round instead of three.
A JSON array at the top level.
The capture predates the thing it captured.
The envelope claims to have been emitted before the payload it references existed.
A data: URI. The reference exists so the bytes travel separately; inlining them defeats the entire boundary.
A correct instant rendered with an offset. It compares correctly and canonicalises differently, which is why only Z is admitted.
A kind outside the closed vocabulary and outside the x- namespace.
A destination hint and a vendor-shaped source member. The envelope is closed, so both fail loudly instead of riding along ignored.
A major version this implementation does not validate.
